title: Longest Common Subsequence
statement: Given two strings `text1` and `text2`, return the length of their longest common subsequence. A subsequence is formed by deleting zero or more characters without changing order.
starter_code:
def longest_common_subsequence(text1, text2):
    # dp[i][j] = LCS of text1[:i] and text2[:j]
    dp = [[0] * (len(text2) + 1) for _ in range(len(text1) + 1)]
    return 0

predict_steps.prompt: When text1[i-1] equals text2[j-1], how do you set dp[i][j]?
predict_steps.hint: Extend the LCS of the prefixes.

predict_steps.prompt: For abcde and ace, what is the LCS length?

viva.question: What does dp[i][j] mean for the LCS of two prefixes?
expected_points: it is the LCS length of text1[:i] and text2[:j]
matching characters take the diagonal plus one
mismatches take the max of skipping either character
filling the table costs time proportional to the product of the lengths

viva.question: What is the LCS length when one string is empty?
expected_points: the first row and first column stay zero
nothing can be matched against an empty prefix
those zeros are the recurrence base

viva.question: Why do equal characters take the diagonal plus one?
expected_points: that match extends a common subsequence by one
the diagonal represents both prefixes without those characters
skipping either character cannot do better than using a real match plus the best before it
the invariant is optimal LCS lengths for all smaller prefixes
